title: Add `miniaudio` audio driver
body:
## Technical overview

- Adds `AudioDriverMiniaudio` as an additional driver without changing the existing `AudioServer` mixing model or removing native drivers.
- Vendors miniaudio 0.11.26 (`dev-0.12` branch) at a fixed commit, with the temporary upstream patch from [miniaudio#1150](https://github.com/mackron/miniaudio/pull/1150).
- Uses separate playback and capture devices, with captured samples transferred through a lock-free ring buffer.
- Coordinates device initialization and recovery from the main thread.
- Temporarily handles WASAPI default-device notifications in Godot due to [miniaudio#1149](https://github.com/mackron/miniaudio/issues/1149).
- Disables miniaudio’s bundled decoders, leaving Godot’s existing decoding paths unchanged.

The driver can be selected with `--audio-driver miniaudio` and in Godot Project Settings.

## What problem(s) does this PR solve?

An SDL-based audio driver encapsulation was partially implemented in #109362, but the implementation remains an incomplete draft. This PR provides an independently developed alternative based on [miniaudio](https://github.com/mackron/miniaudio).

The initial `miniaudio` audio driver implementation preserves Godot’s `AudioServer` and mixing model. On Windows it has been tested with output and input device selection, default and per-application rerouting, changes between stereo and surround devices, hot plugging, input-buffer synchronization, device invalidation, and recovery after another application acquires and releases exclusive control.

This PR does not propose replacing the existing drivers immediately. Its purpose is to evaluate whether a shared audio-device layer can provide more consistent behavior with less platform-specific Godot code.

The motivation behind this and the problems it solves closely match ["Replace the audio drivers with SDL"
proposal](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/12908)

**Related issues addressed when using the `miniaudio` driver:**
- #75603
- #18732

**Other issues `miniaudio` driver may address:**
- #109055
- #84699
- #80173
- #119298

**Several long-running efforts to add or replace individual platform drivers that this PR potentially addresses**:
- Android low-latency audio: [Oboe proposal #2358](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/2358) and [draft PR #109120](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/109120). The Oboe PR includes device-switching and stream-recovery work similar to what this PR implements.
- Native PipeWire: [proposal #10723](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/10723) and [PR #111056](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/111056).
- JACK: [PR #35613](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/35613), open since 2020.
- OpenBSD sndio: [proposal #3097](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/3097).

**There is one important exception**: `miniaudio` has no native PipeWire backend. Therefore it does not eliminate the rationale for Godot’s PipeWire PR. On Linux it would currently use PulseAudio, ALSA or JACK.

If `AudioDriver` eventually converges on a single `miniaudio` implementation, a native PipeWire backend could still be added through `miniaudio`'s [Custom backend](https://miniaud.io/docs/examples/custom_backend.html) interface, reusing the device-switching and recovery logic implemented here.

## Additional information

`miniaudio` currently supports the following backends:

- WASAPI
- DirectSound
- WinMM
- Core Audio (Apple)
- ALSA
- PulseAudio
- JACK
- sndio (OpenBSD)
- audio(4) (NetBSD and OpenBSD)
- OSS (FreeBSD)
- AAudio (Android 8.0+)
- OpenSL|ES (Android only)
- Web Audio (Emscripten)
- Null (Silence)
- **Custom**: proprietary console backends can be integrated via `miniaudio`'s [Custom backend](https://miniaud.io/docs/examples/custom_backend.html) interface.

### `miniaudio` could enable later
- `AudioServer.restart()` to use when audio system has failed or settings have changed: [proposal #14962](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/14962) 
- Multiple simultaneous capture devices: [proposal #2915](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/2915). `miniaudio` can create multiple devices, however currently Godot’s `AudioDriver` and `AudioServer` APIs assume one input.
- Multiple output devices or per-bus device routing: [proposal #1867](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/1867). 
- Enumerating/selecting the underlying audio backend: [proposal #9858](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/9858). `miniaudio` already has an explicit backend abstraction and backend selection API, though exposing it through Godot would be separate API work.

#### Decoders

Godot already uses [dr_libs](https://github.com/mackron/dr_libs) from the same author for `mp3` decoding. `dr_libs` are embedded in `miniaudio` (disabled in this PR).

With `miniaudio` `dr_libs` dependency can be eventually removed. `miniaudio` also has `flac` and `wav`, which can be used via the same [decoding interface](https://miniaud.io/docs/manual/index.html#Decoding) as `mp3`.

There's already a PR for `wav`: #96545 

### Third-party dependency

This does introduce a third-party dependency. Unlike SDL, its exclusive focus is audio.
`miniaudio` is well-established audio library used in variety of projects, including game engines. 

Notable users include:
- [raylib](https://github.com/raysan5/raylib/blob/master/HISTORY.md#notes-on-raylib-20)
- [Orx Engine](https://github.com/orx/orx)
- [O3DE](https://www.docs.o3de.org/docs/user-guide/gems/reference/audio/miniaudio/miniaudio/)

### Drawbacks

- SDL is already vendored by Godot for joypads, while `miniaudio` would be a new dependency (except `dr_libs` excerpt already used in Godot).
- Godot will inherit upstream behavior and upstream bugs.
- This PR's Windows notification handling workaround shows the integration does not eliminate all platform-specific code, but it substantially reduces it. An [upstream `miniaudio` issue](https://github.com/mackron/miniaudio/issues/1149) has been filed, so the rerouting workaround may be removable once the upstream fixes are available and validated.
- Currently all the testing has been done on Windows.
- Maintaining `miniaudio` alongside all native drivers indefinitely could increase total maintenance. An optional evaluation period followed by an explicit long-term decision could be the plan.

## LLM Usage

LLM was used to research issues, proposals, PRs, and discussions relevant to Godot's audio driver implementation, and potential use of a third-party library. All the information and links were validated and scrutinized by me.

LLM was also used for a preliminary code review. All the code was developed and written by me.
